deep_dive.executive_summary: At $50.27 (Yahoo close 2026-08-07), our base case annual return is -24.36% per year over seven years on filing-normalized owner earnings of $0.92 per share, net of $18.86 billion of debt. CSX remains a duopoly-class eastern railroad with $14.1 billion of FY2025 revenue and $1.0 billion of cash. Normalized owner earnings of $1.71 billion support dividends and reinvestment, but leverage is nearly double what the stale debt fact had implied. Component proof base value is $7.12 per share. Moat is unproven pending a full competitive-advantage review; dhando is pending. Proposed stance: watch.

change_control.rule: A source fact is locked. Every assumption change requires a reason, author, timestamp, and before/after value.

method_fit.label: High-return compounder
applicability_tests: Owner earnings can be separated from stock compensation, working capital, and maintenance capital.
Incremental returns on retained capital are observable and durable.
The competitive advantage explains pricing, retention, share, or cost outcomes.
Terminal value is supported by a reinvestment runway rather than an unexplained multiple.
failure_modes: growth projected without its capital cost
terminal value unsupported by a durable mechanism

validation_cohort.purpose: Test depletion, commodity exposure, finite reserves, and royalty-unit reconciliation.
Test tangible capital, credit losses, funding, regulation, and excess-capital realization.
Test owner earnings, capital-light reinvestment, cyclicality, and buyback value creation.
Test normalized margins, industry supply response, replacement cost, and reinvestment timing.
Test product concentration, pipeline probabilities, patent cliffs, and catalyst timing.

method_fit.rule: Use one primary method and no more than two corroborating methods; irrelevant methods and personas remain silent.

outcomes.weighting_rule: Do not change a persona's relevance within a power zone until at least 20 attributable, dividend-aware outcomes exist there; never reweight automatically.

attribution.explanation: The current component schedule is the first decision-grade baseline; attribution begins with the next dated valuation snapshot.

Q2 2026 balance sheet shows $18.9B total debt (current plus non-current lease-adjusted obligations) versus a stale 2012 LongTermDebt tag that had understated leverage by ~$9B.
FY2025 10-K filed: revenue $14.1B (down 3% YoY), operating cash flow $4.6B, capital spending $2.9B.
FY2025 normalized owner earnings $1.71B (operating cash flow minus capital spending) anchors reinvestment DCF proof.
Joe Boitnott became President and CEO after prior leadership transitions; capital allocation and service metrics under new team.
Continued precision-scheduled railroading and industrial development pipeline (~600 projects cited in 2026 proxy) to grow on-network freight.
Activist DFAN14A termination notice on file; prior Mantle Ridge campaign context remains in third-party activist folder.
Surface Transportation Board oversight of Class I mergers and service standards continues to shape Eastern rail competitive structure with Norfolk Southern.
Hunter Harrison-era precision scheduled railroading transformed CSX operating model; legacy efficiency culture persists in investor narrative.

industry.structure: U.S. Class I freight railroad oligopoly in the Eastern U.S.; CSX and Norfolk Southern dominate east-of-Mississippi interchange with high fixed-cost networks and limited new entry.
industry.share_shift: Intermodal and merchandise carloads shift with truck competition and port volumes; CSX gains when on-network industrial development converts to carloads.
industry.trend: Precision scheduled railroading, fuel efficiency, and labor productivity offset cyclical industrial and coal decline; capital spending near $2.9B annually maintains track and equipment.
